title: The Robot That Never Gets Tired
blurb: Where the word robot came from, how a machine senses and moves, and why picking up a sock is harder than chess.

title: The Rocket That Throws Itself Away
blurb: Fire pushes down, the rocket goes up, and most of the machine gets dropped along the way.

title: The Bird That Knows When Dawn Is Coming
blurb: The rooster crows before the sun comes up, and he is not guessing. He is running a clock.

title: The Rose That Never Had Thorns
blurb: Those sharp points are prickles, not thorns. And the rose is a close cousin of the apple.

title: The Man Who Gave the Sandwich Its Name
blurb: Two slices of bread, one very busy Earl, and the machine that put sliced bread in every American kitchen.

title: The Machine That Is Always Falling
blurb: A satellite does not hover. It falls forever, missing the Earth by exactly the right amount, and that is how it stays up.

title: The Planet That Would Float
blurb: Saturn is lighter than water, wears rings made of billions of ice chunks, and hides a six-sided storm at its pole.

title: The Bus That Had to Be Yellow
blurb: Every school bus in America is the same exact shade of yellow, and the reason was decided in one room in 1939.

title: The Scorpion That Glows in the Dark
blurb: An animal older than trees, nearly blind, that hunts by feeling the ground and shines blue-green under ultraviolet light.

title: The Turtle That Never Forgets the Way Home
blurb: A green sea turtle can cross an ocean, wait thirty years, and still find the exact beach where it hatched.

title: The Fish Where the Dad Has the Babies
blurb: The slowest fish in the ocean has a square tail, no stomach, and a father who gives birth.

title: The Seal That Sees With Its Whiskers
blurb: A seal can chase a fish it never saw, by feeling the trail the fish left behind in the water.

title: The Seed That Packs Its Own Lunch
blurb: Inside every seed is a tiny folded-up plant and a packed lunch to get it to the light.

title: The Shark That Never Stops Growing Teeth
blurb: The fish with no bones, a body wrapped in tiny teeth, and a family older than the first tree.

title: The Sheep That Never Stops Growing Its Coat
blurb: Wild sheep drop their wool every spring. We bred that out, and now the woolliest animal on Earth needs a haircut to stay alive.

title: The Skeleton That Rebuilds Itself
blurb: The 206 bones inside you are alive, and they tear themselves down and build themselves back up your whole life.

title: The Skunk That Warns You First
blurb: The animal that carries only six sprays, so it spends all its effort making sure it never has to use one.

title: The Sloth That Is Slow on Purpose
blurb: The upside-down animal that moves slowly to stay alive, grows a garden in its fur, and climbs down its tree only once a week.

title: The Snail That Cannot Leave Its House
blurb: The slow one that grows its own shell, walks on glue, and eats with fourteen thousand teeth.

title: The Snake That Smells With Its Tongue
blurb: The legless hunter that smells in stereo, swallows meals wider than its own head, and reads body heat in the dark.

title: The Snowflake That Started as Dust
blurb: Every snow crystal grows six arms around a speck of dust, and the big ones have never once repeated.

title: The Little Trick Hiding in a Bar of Soap
blurb: Water cannot wash grease away on its own. Soap is the go-between that makes it happen, and people have been boiling it from fat and ashes for four thousand years.

title: The Panel That Eats Sunlight
blurb: A sheet of doped sand with no moving parts that turns light straight into electricity, and now makes the cheapest power in history.

title: Eight Worlds Around One Star
blurb: How a cold cloud of dust became a sun, eight planets, and a whole lot of leftovers.

title: The House That Never Stops Falling
blurb: People have lived above your head every single day since 2000, in a machine that falls forever and always misses.

title: The Spider That Makes Its Own Rope
blurb: Eight legs, a belly full of liquid protein, and a thread that beats steel for its weight.

title: The Squirrel That Plants a Forest by Forgetting
blurb: The nut-burying neighbor that remembers thousands of hiding places, fakes a few, and grows oak trees by accident.

title: The Star That Made You
blurb: Every star is a giant ball of hot gas building new atoms in its core, and almost every atom in your body came out of one.

title: The Star That Is Not a Fish
blurb: No brain, no blood, no bones. It runs on seawater and walks on hundreds of tiny feet.

title: The Dinosaur With a Roof on Its Back
blurb: Seventeen plates, four tail spikes named after a comic strip, and a brain the size of a lime.

title: The Bug That Pretends to Be a Twig
blurb: An insect shaped like a stick, with eggs disguised as seeds and a species that came back from the dead.

title: The Ray That Cannot See Its Own Dinner
blurb: Its eyes are on top and its mouth is underneath, so a stingray finds buried crabs by feeling the electricity in their muscles.

title: The Bag of Acid That Never Burns You
blurb: Your stomach holds acid strong enough to dissolve metal, and rebuilds its own lining every few days to survive it.

title: The Berry That Is Not a Berry
blurb: The red part is not the fruit, the dots are, and the whole thing was invented by accident three hundred years ago.

title: The Boat That Sinks on Purpose
blurb: The boat that floods itself to dive, listens instead of looking, and makes its own air out of the sea.

title: The Star We Live Next To
blurb: Our nearest star: how it makes light, why its sunbeams are older than you think, and how people learned what it is made of without ever touching it.

title: The Flower That Follows the Sun
blurb: It looks like one big flower. It is really a thousand tiny ones, packed at the only angle that never repeats.

title: The Gray Baby That Turned Into a Swan
blurb: The bird that hatches gray and fuzzy, carries more neck bones than a giraffe, and once proved a whole continent wrong.

title: The King That Crunched Bones
blurb: The tyrant lizard king: a bite that broke through bone, eyes that looked straight ahead, and two small arms nobody has explained yet.

title: The Devil That Screams in the Dark
blurb: The loudest little scavenger in Australia, the strongest bite for its size of any mammal, and a cancer that learned to travel.

title: The Teacher Who Waits Three Seconds
blurb: Why the best teachers ask more than they tell, and how three seconds of silence changes what a kid can say.

title: The Bear the President Would Not Shoot
blurb: A bad hunting trip, a newspaper cartoon, and a German workshop turned into the toy on every kid's bed.

title: The Hardest Thing in Your Body
blurb: Enamel is harder than bone, your body only makes it once, and your teeth are quietly keeping a record of your whole life.

title: The Tube That Looks Back in Time
blurb: A tube of glass that showed the moon has mountains, and that we are not at the center of anything.

title: The Little Tube That Measures Heat
blurb: How a thin glass tube turned a feeling into a number, and why it only ever tells you about itself.

title: The Tiger With Stripes on Its Skin
blurb: The biggest cat alive. Its stripes go all the way down to its skin, and no two tigers wear the same pattern.

title: The Only Part of You That Cannot Heal Itself
blurb: Enamel is the hardest thing your body makes, it can never grow back, and it quietly keeps a record of the day you were born.

title: The Brush That Fights an Invisible City
blurb: Two minutes of soft bristles tears apart a living city of bacteria, and it took people five thousand years to get the design right.

title: The Storm That Touches the Ground
blurb: The spinning column of air that hangs out of a thundercloud, and why it only counts once it reaches the grass.

title: The Tortoise That Wears Its Bones on the Outside
blurb: The slow land reptile whose shell is really its own ribs and backbone, and who can outlive six human generations.

title: The Toucan and Its Impossible Bill
blurb: The bird that carries a bill a third of its own length, and how scientists finally worked out what it is for.

title: The Tractor That Was Built to Be Slow
blurb: The machine that trades speed for pulling force, and the one clever hitch that stopped it flipping over backward.

title: The Train That Steers Itself
blurb: No steering wheel, no driver turning the wheels, and a clever cone shape that walks a train around every curve.

title: The Chest With the Secret Keyhole
blurb: Pirates almost never buried gold. The real treasure chests had a fake keyhole on the front and a hidden one in the lid.

title: The Tree That Drinks With Its Feet
blurb: Roots that drink, a trunk that lifts water higher than a building with no pump, and leaves that build wood out of thin air.

title: The Tree That Eats Air
blurb: A tree builds its whole body out of air, water, and sunlight, and keeps a diary of every year it lived inside its own wood.

title: Three Horns and a Shield of Bone
blurb: The three horned giant that carried a solid slab of bone on its head, and was still standing on the last day of the dinosaurs.

title: The Truck That Brings You Everything
blurb: Why a big rig is really two machines, how it stops with air, and the trucker whose idea rearranged the world.

title: Nobody Grows a Vegetable
blurb: Every vegetable is a different body part of a plant, and the word itself is something people made up in the kitchen.

title: The Wooden Box That Sings
blurb: Seventy pieces of wood, a stick strung with horsehair, and a sound that carries to the back of the hall.

title: The Walrus That Walks on Its Teeth
blurb: The tooth walker of the Arctic: it hooks itself onto ice with its tusks, finds clams by touch in the dark, and blushes pink when it gets warm.

title: The Water That Keeps Coming Back
blurb: No water on Earth is new. The rain in your yard has been an ocean, a cloud, and a dinosaur's drink, and it is still going around.

title: The Waterfall That Walks Backward
blurb: Falling water eats the rock underneath it, so every waterfall slowly climbs upstream. Niagara has walked seven miles.

title: The Watermelon That Came From the Desert
blurb: A dry-country vine that builds its own water tank, and how a pale, bitter gourd became the sweetest thing on the picnic table.

title: The Biggest Animal That Ever Lived
blurb: The blue whale is larger than any dinosaur, breathes air like you do, and its family once walked on land.

title: The Machine That Catches the Wind
blurb: Three blades that work like airplane wings, tips moving faster than a race car, turning moving air into the electricity in your lamp.

title: The Windmill That Turns Wind Into Bread
blurb: A building with no engine and no fuel. It catches the wind, grinds grain into flour, and has been doing it for a thousand years.

title: The Wolf Pack Is Just a Family
blurb: The howl, the pups, and the alpha wolf that never existed. A wolf pack turns out to be a mom, a dad, and their kids.

title: The Wombat That Poops in Cubes
blurb: The burrowing Australian marsupial with a backward pouch, an armored backside, and the only cube-shaped droppings in nature.

title: The Bird That Hammers All Day
blurb: The bird that drills into trees twenty times a second, catches grubs with a tongue that wraps around its own skull, and builds homes for half the forest.

title: The Worm That Built the Ground
blurb: The eyeless, boneless animal that eats dirt, breathes through its skin, and quietly builds the soil every plant on land grows in.

title: The Zebra Nobody Could Tame
blurb: Every zebra wears a stripe pattern no other zebra has, and in ten thousand years nobody has managed to tame one.
